summary: In Greek mythology, Eusorus (Ancient Greek: Εὔσωρος; Homer Εὐσσώρου) was the father of the Thracian captain Acamas, who with Peirous led the Thracians enclosed by the Hellespont as Trojan allies — kept distinct in this atlas from Eusorus father of Cyzicus in the Argonautica.

sections.heading: Father of Acamas
paragraphs: Homer's Catalogue sets Acamas and Peirous at the head of the Thracians and names Acamas the valiant son of Eüssorus. When Agamemnon broke the Trojan ranks at the opening of Iliad 6, he smote Eüssorus' son through the horn of his horse-hair crest. Apollodorus likewise lists Acamas son of Eusorus among the Thracians who joined Troy after nine years of siege.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (eusorus-thracian) is the Thracian father of Acamas in Homer and Apollodorus. Distinct from Eusorus (or Aeneus' father-in-law) in Apollonius, Hyginus, and the Orphic Argonautica, whose daughter Aenete bore Cyzicus of the Doliones — a Propontis house the Wikipedia stub sometimes conflates with the Thracian line.
